meta.title: A Dollar for May
meta.textType: dialogue: the context of a chat

paragraphs: On Saturday morning, Lily and May walked into a small fruit shop. A sign on the door said "SALE: Two Bags for Fifty Baht." The shop was full of shoppers, and the air smelled sweet. The girls wanted some fruit for the Explorers' meeting. Lily held a small list, and May held a blue purse. A woman stood at the counter with a dollar in her hand. She looked at the fruit and then at the woman behind the counter.

"How much is this bag?" asked the woman with the dollar. "The price is thirty baht," said the woman behind the counter. "I only have this," said the woman with the dollar. Her English was good, but her voice was soft. "I am sorry, we do not take dollars," said the woman behind the counter. "You must pay in baht."

The woman with the dollar turned to Lily and May. "I am a visitor from another country," she said. "Is there a place near here to change money?" Lily thought for a moment. "The bank is on the other side of the town," said Lily. "It is far, and the road is busy," said May. May looked at the dollar and had an idea. "I collect money from other countries," she said. "Can I have your dollar, and I will pay for your fruit?"

The visitor smiled. "That is very kind," she said. "Yes, of course." "The sale is good," said the woman behind the counter. "Do you want two bags?" "Yes, please," said the visitor. May took fifty baht from her purse and put it on the counter.

The woman behind the counter used a small machine and gave May a small paper. "Here is your receipt," she said. "Thank you," said May. The visitor gave the dollar to May, and May put it carefully in her purse. "Keep the receipt with the dollar," said Lily. "Then you can remember today," she said.

The visitor took her two bags of fruit and said, "Thank you, both of you." She gave each girl a banana from the bag. May smiled at her new dollar, and Lily smiled at May. Nobody in the shop spoke for a moment. The woman behind the counter smiled at the girls too. Then the shoppers began to talk again.
